title: Building a Door That Teaches Translation
description: From Point_One you learned position. Now watch how movement is built — not as free motion, but as constrained displacement along axes.
concept_layer: displacement, translation, axis constraint, sequential phases

capture_leaks.rotation: Trans_Rotation — translation changes position without changing orientation; rotation is a different beast
capture_leaks.scale: Trans_Scale — translation preserves size; scale transforms extent
capture_leaks.composition: Trans_AxisDecomposition — sequential constraint is not general transform composition; matrices compose differently
capture_leaks.path_vs_displacement: forces, swarmintelligence — translation is the end state, not the journey; trajectories, paths, and flows need different representation
capture_leaks.reversibility_assumption: foundationscrisis — translation is invertible (you can undo it); many real transformations are not

limit: Translation moves without turning, without growing, without remembering the path. Each axis is independent only because we chose it so. In the real world, your arm cannot move along X without rotating at the shoulder. The abstraction isolates what life entangles.

stages.title: Position can be changed
stages.thinking: In Point_One, you held a point and saw its coordinates. But the point only moved because your hand moved it. What if the code moves it? Translation is position + displacement. A Vector3 added to a Vector3.
stages.code:
# A point has position
var position: Vector3 = Vector3(5.0, 2.0, 3.0)

# Translation is adding a displacement
var displacement: Vector3 = Vector3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# The new position
position += displacement  # Vector3(6.0, 2.0, 3.0)

# Displacement is not a place. It has no address.
# It exists only as difference, as change.

stages.title: Give it a body to move
stages.thinking: Just like the point needed a sphere to be seen, translation needs a physical object to be felt. We build a door — a panel you can grab and slide. The door makes displacement tangible.

stages.title: Constrain to one axis
stages.thinking: Free movement teaches nothing. If the door could go anywhere, there would be no lesson. By constraining motion to the Y axis first, then X, the player discovers that translation has direction. You cannot open this door by pushing sideways — only by pulling up.
stages.code:
extends Node3D

signal goal_reached

@export var target_y: float = 0.25
@export var target_x: float = -0.5

var _phase: int = 0  # 0=locked, 1=slide_up, 2=slide_sideways
var _start_pos: Vector3
var _is_grabbed := false

func _on_knob_grabbed() -> void:
	_is_grabbed = true
	_start_pos = position
	if _phase == 0:
		_phase = 1  # Begin upward phase

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if not _is_grabbed:
		return
	
	match _phase:
		1:  # Only Y movement allowed
			position.x = _start_pos.x  # Lock X
			position.z = _start_pos.z  # Lock Z
			if position.y >= target_y:
				_phase = 2  # Unlock sideways
		2:  # Only X movement allowed
			position.y = target_y  # Lock Y at target
			position.z = _start_pos.z  # Lock Z

stages.title: Show the path
stages.thinking: The player needs to see where the door wants to go before they grab it. Arrow indicators drawn with ImmediateMesh show the two-phase path: up first, then sideways. The arrows are the displacement vector made visible — direction and magnitude as geometry.
stages.code:
func _create_path_indicators() -> void:
	var arrow_z = door_depth + 0.08
	
	# Phase 1: UP arrow
	_create_path_arrow(
		Vector3(0, knob_height, arrow_z),
		Vector3(0, knob_height + target_y, arrow_z),
		Color(0.8, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7)
	)
	_create_label("1.Up", Vector3(0.15, knob_height + target_y/2, arrow_z))
	
	# Phase 2: SIDEWAYS arrow
	_create_path_arrow(
		Vector3(0, knob_height + target_y, arrow_z),
		Vector3(-door_width, knob_height + target_y, arrow_z),
		Color(0.8, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7)
	)
	_create_label("2.Slide", Vector3(-door_width/2, knob_height + target_y + 0.1, arrow_z))

func _create_path_arrow(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, color: Color) -> void:
	var mesh_instance = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var immediate_mesh = ImmediateMesh.new()
	immediate_mesh.surface_begin(Mesh.PRIMITIVE_LINES)
	immediate_mesh.surface_add_vertex(from)
	immediate_mesh.surface_add_vertex(to)
	immediate_mesh.surface_end()
	mesh_instance.mesh = immediate_mesh

stages.title: Two doors mirror each other
stages.thinking: One door teaches constraint. Two doors teach symmetry. The left door slides up then left. The right door slides up then right. Same operation, opposite displacement. Translation doesn’t care about position — only about the vector you add.
stages.code:
func _create_doors() -> void:
	var door_gap = 0.02
	var door_offset = door_width / 2 + door_gap
	
	# Left door: slides UP then LEFT
	_left_door = _create_constrained_door(
		"LeftDoor",
		Vector3(-door_offset, 0.0, 0.0),
		Color(0.8, 0.3, 0.3),  # Red
		target_y,
		-(door_width + door_gap)  # Negative X = left
	)
	
	# Right door: slides UP then RIGHT
	_right_door = _create_constrained_door(
		"RightDoor",
		Vector3(door_offset, 0.0, 0.0),
		Color(0.3, 0.3, 0.8),  # Blue
		target_y,
		(door_width + door_gap)  # Positive X = right
	)

stages.title: The wireframe container
stages.thinking: The doors live inside a wireframe cube — visible edges, invisible faces. The container defines the space that translation operates within. Without boundaries, displacement would have no reference. The cube is the coordinate system the doors move inside.
stages.code:
func _setup_container() -> void:
	_container = Node3D.new()
	add_child(_container)
	
	# 12 edges of a cube
	var edges = [
		[Vector3(-0.5, 0, -0.5), Vector3(0.5, 0, -0.5)],
		[Vector3(0.5, 0, -0.5), Vector3(0.5, 0, 0.5)],
		[Vector3(0.5, 0, 0.5), Vector3(-0.5, 0, 0.5)],
		[Vector3(-0.5, 0, 0.5), Vector3(-0.5, 0, -0.5)],
		# ... 4 top edges, 4 vertical edges ...
	]
	
	for edge in edges:
		_create_edge_line(edge[0] * cube_size, edge[1] * cube_size)

func _create_edge_line(from: Vector3, to: Vector3) -> void:
	var material = StandardMaterial3D.new()
	material.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
	material.albedo_color = Color(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3)
	material.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA

stages.title: Completion as event
stages.thinking: Both doors must open for the puzzle to complete. This is the first time code reacts to the player finishing something — a signal fires when each door reaches its target, and a check function tests if both are done. Translation becomes a goal, not just a motion.

stages.title: Give it identity
stages.thinking: The code is complete. Two constrained doors inside a wireframe cube. The identity tells us what it knows about itself: translation requires both a direction and a magnitude. Constraint is what makes it meaningful. Without the lock on axes, there would be nothing to learn.
stages.code:
# @identity
# essence: constrained_translation — move only on allowed axis
# desire: learner physically discovers that translation is axis-specific
# critical_parameter: the axis sequence constraint — UP must complete before SIDEWAYS unlocks
# triggers: grabbing the knob and moving; axis deviation is corrected
# emerges: the idea that translation has direction — not all displacement is allowed
# needs: two grabbable door knobs [has]
# relationships: precursor to axis_translation_cube
# truth: a translation requires both a direction and a magnitude — constraint is what makes it meaningful
